title: Input and output: `io.Reader`, `io.Writer` and composing them

videos.script: This is the first lesson of the course's second half. The first half ran many things at once. This half is the standard library those things are built from. {{doc}} It starts with two interfaces, each with one method. A Reader fills a slice of bytes. A Writer takes one. Files, network connections and HTTP bodies are all one or the other. {{read}} You call Read by hand once, eight bytes at a time, and see the end arrive as an error called EOF. Then you write a Reader of your own, and it hands back its last six letters and EOF in the same call. {{write}} Next, one report function and three destinations: the terminal, a buffer, and a hash. The function never changes. {{pipe}} Last, the pieces that plug together. A goroutine writes into a pipe, and one copy feeds a hash, the terminal and a string at once. {{close}} Lesson 18 opens real files.
